cards.back: The place where a plant or animal lives.
cards.say: habitat. The place where a plant or animal lives. A pond is a habitat.

cards.back: A feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat.
cards.say: adaptation. A feature that helps a living thing survive in its habitat. Thick fur is an adaptation to the cold.

cards.back: An animal that hunts other animals for food.
cards.say: predator. An animal that hunts other animals for food. A lion is a predator.

cards.back: An animal that is hunted for food.
cards.say: prey. An animal that is hunted for food. A rabbit is prey for a fox.

cards.back: A living thing that makes its own food, such as a plant.
cards.say: producer. A living thing that makes its own food, such as a plant.

cards.back: A living thing that eats other living things.
cards.say: consumer. A living thing that eats other living things. A rabbit is a consumer.

cards.back: An animal with a backbone.
cards.say: vertebrate. An animal with a backbone. A fish is a vertebrate.

cards.back: An animal with no backbone.
cards.say: invertebrate. An animal with no backbone. A snail is an invertebrate.

cards.back: A state of matter that keeps its shape.
cards.say: solid. A state of matter that keeps its shape. A stone is a solid.

cards.back: A state of matter that flows.
cards.say: liquid. A state of matter that flows. Milk is a liquid.

cards.back: A state of matter that spreads out to fill its container.
cards.say: gas. A state of matter that spreads out to fill its container. Air is a gas.

cards.back: To change from a liquid to a gas.
cards.say: evaporate. To change from a liquid to a gas. Puddles evaporate in the sun.

cards.back: To change from a gas to a liquid.
cards.say: condense. To change from a gas to a liquid. Steam condenses on a cold window.

cards.back: A material that lets heat or electricity pass through easily.
cards.say: conductor. A material that lets heat or electricity pass through easily. Copper is a conductor.

cards.back: A material that does not let heat or electricity pass through easily.
cards.say: insulator. A material that does not let heat or electricity pass through easily. Rubber is an insulator.

cards.back: A path that electricity flows around.
cards.say: circuit. A path that electricity flows around. A circuit has a cell, wires and a bulb.

cards.back: A quick movement backwards and forwards that makes sound.
cards.say: vibration. A quick movement backwards and forwards that makes sound. A plucked guitar string makes a vibration.

cards.back: How high or low a sound is.
cards.say: pitch. How high or low a sound is. A whistle has a high pitch.

cards.back: How loud or quiet a sound is.
cards.say: volume. How loud or quiet a sound is. A whisper has a low volume.

cards.back: The path of one object around another in space.
cards.say: orbit. The path of one object around another in space. The Moon orbits the Earth.

cards.back: A tiny piece that materials are made from.
cards.say: particle. A tiny piece that materials are made from. A drop of water has billions of particles.

cards.back: What makes things happen, such as moving, heating and lighting.
cards.say: energy. What makes things happen, such as moving, heating and lighting. We get energy from food.

cards.back: A medicine that protects the body against a disease.
cards.say: vaccine. A medicine that protects the body against a disease. A vaccine protects you from measles.

cards.back: A body part that pulls on bones to make them move.
cards.say: muscle. A body part that pulls on bones to make them move. Your biceps is a muscle.

cards.back: The hard outer layer of a tooth.
cards.say: enamel. The hard outer layer of a tooth. Enamel protects the tooth.
